items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: so you’d see Jerome Richardson’s on this one

ctx.x: No. It’s what I wanted to do from an early age. I mean as soon as I could read I was reading the backs of the albums or reading the labels on the 78s that my father had. And I was just fascinated, you know, usually somebody’s liner notes, Orrin Keepnews or George Avakian or Nat Hentoff or someone you know and I would read the whole thing beginning to end and then read about the session if they had session details and then look at the credits. Oh my God Tony Williams on drums, Jo Jones on drums or whoever the…

It’s interesting you say that because I used to do the same thing. I was more attuned to the saxophone players so you’d see Jerome Richardson’s on this one, and now I notice he’s on that one and all these people like playing musical chairs and said, wow, I want to do that.

Yeah. Exactly. At that early age, you know, 12, 13, I had my own bands already at school but when I saw Grady Tate, when I saw his name on an album and then saw his name on another album or I saw Joe Dukes’ name on an album and then hear him in another context, you know hear him with Jack McDuff or Grady Tate with Jimmy Smith and then
